name: llama.cpp
what: The reference GGUF inference engine. llama-server serves one model per process over an OpenAI-style API with every knob exposed on the command line; started with --models-dir (or --models-preset) it is a router instead, starting one child llama-server per model it is asked to load.

detect.note: a unit is proposed from a running llama-server (its -m and --port), since there is no configuration file convention. A router (GET /props says role router) gives one unit per model in its GET /models; its children, on ports of their own, are not units. Ollama's runner is a llama-server too (lib/ollama/llama-server) and belongs to Ollama. A server a systemd user unit keeps is started and stopped through that unit.

endpoints.router models: GET /models (each model's status and its child's argv)

can: start a unit with its recorded argv
treat it as loaded while it answers /health
a router: load and unload each model through its API; see a child busy in its /slots
cannot: a single server: unload without stopping (one model for the server's life)
change the context without a restart
a router: stop it from the page (it serves every model; its own unit stops it)

never: --host 0.0.0.0 without a reverse proxy in front: there is no login

update.note: Releases were build numbers (b1234) and are now versions (v0.9.0); --version gives the version on a new build and the build on an old one. Download the archive that matches your CUDA, Vulkan or CPU and replace the folder; the check compares the installed version to the newest release.

windows: Download llama-<build>-bin-win-cuda-<cuda>-x64.zip (and the matching cudart zip) from the releases page, unpack beside each other, put the folder on PATH.
linux: Download the matching tarball, or build: cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON && cmake --build build --config Release -j

good: any GGUF, any quant, exact control of layers, context and KV types
not: switching between models without restarting, unless it runs as a router
a store, a pull command, or a UI: bring your own
